$comment: Standing campaign rule, from #21's round-2 gauntlet: a mutation claim ships
with a committed, re-runnable mutant list and its results, or it is not
evidence. Round 2's write-up claimed '25 run, 25 caught' with nothing in the
repo a reviewer could execute, and that is a number, not a receipt.
Gate it:  node packages/core/mutants/run.mjs --check   (exit 1 if any survives)
Each mutant is a single verbatim substitution in one source file. The runner
refuses a mutant whose `find` does not occur exactly once, so a mutant that
has drifted out of the code is a loud failure rather than a silent pass — the
failure mode a ledger like this actually has.
`catches` names the tests that must go red. It is checked, not decorative:
the runner asserts every listed name appears among the failures, so a mutant
that is caught by some unrelated test counts as an escape.

mutants.why: Reads a line break as \n alone again, which is the same defect `\s` had for whitespace one function over: U+0085 NEL, U+2028 and U+2029 end a line everywhere a line is rendered and `\n` sees none of them. A body whose breaks are NEL becomes one line, so a reply-blockquote on its first line swallows the author's own words and a multi-sentence body reads as a single sentence. Found by this round running its own `\p{White_Space}` fix back over the rest of the package.
catches: reads a line break the way every renderer does, not the way a newline does
